name: the OpenAI SDK
title: OpenAI SDK integration: replay logs on cheaper or newer models
description: Point rightmodeler at your OpenAI SDK request log: it replays recorded calls through cheaper or newer models and measures each output against what you accepted.
lede: No tracing platform required. rightmodeler reads the request and response log your code already writes around the OpenAI SDK, measures cheaper or newer candidates against accepted outputs, and reports the result call by call.
tldr: rightmodeler reads per-line OpenAI SDK request and response dumps with a dedicated adapter: each logged call becomes a step, with no tracing platform in between. Lines are recognized by a messages array beside a response object carrying choices, grouped into trajectories by case_id and ordered by timestamp. Successful steps are replayed against cheaper or newer candidates through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure and scored against the answer you already shipped.

steps.label: 01 · Log
steps.title: Dump requests and responses as JSONL
steps.body: Each line holds one call: a case_id naming the run it belongs to, the request's model and messages, and the response object with its choices and usage, the shape you get from dumping your chat.completions kwargs alongside response.model_dump(). If your agent already writes such a log, adding case_id is the only change. Save it anywhere on disk.

steps.label: 02 · Ingest
steps.title: Autodetected, flat, one call per step
steps.body: The adapter recognizes the format from a messages array next to a response object with choices, and requires case_id on every line. Lines sharing a case_id become one trajectory in timestamp order, the system messages are split out into the step's system prompt, the rest become its messages, and choices[0].message becomes the output. usage.prompt_tokens and usage.completion_tokens supply usage from the line or the response, whichever carries them.

steps.label: 03 · Replay + judge
steps.title: Cheaper or newer candidates, judged against what you shipped
steps.body: Recorded steps are replayed against cheaper or newer candidates through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you name with --base-url and --api-key-env. A configured external evaluator scores the outputs when it is reachable; otherwise the built-in judge runs two temperature-zero calls with the reference and candidate positions swapped, choosing a judge from a family that is neither the candidate's nor the reference's. Verdicts rest on statistical lower bounds kept separate per evaluator kind.

steps.label: 04 · Confirm
steps.title: Coupled steps re-run in a container
steps.body: A step whose output can feed later model-authored steps is not judged from the log alone. rightmodeler runs your pipeline inside a container image you name in a --modeb-config file, mounting your app read-only and mapping each scanner step to the runtime header your app emits. Every model call leaves through a metered proxy that swaps the model per step and fails closed on a request with no correlation header, so the candidate does the real work and the spend is accounted for.

steps.label: 05 · Report + apply
steps.title: A per-step report, then a pull request
steps.body: The run writes report.md with a verdict per step family, rightmodeler report --output json prints the full JSON report from the local store, and --output jsonl streams events as the run works. Thin evidence produces an abstention with a named reason. When a family clears every release gate, rightmodeler apply opens a draft pull request that changes model identifiers and nothing else, watch reconciles it against CI, and rollback opens another pull request that restores the pre-apply files, refusing unless every restored digest matches.

setup.intro: Nothing to install: npx runs the published CLI. Hand it your request log. Nothing talks to your OpenAI account; rightmodeler runs on the JSONL files already on your disk.

useCases.title: Validate swaps with no tracing platform
useCases.body: You do not need LangSmith, Langfuse, or an OTel collector to validate a swap to a cheaper or newer model. A plain JSONL log of your OpenAI SDK calls is enough for the full per-step treatment: replay, score, verdict, report, draft pull request.

useCases.title: Measure a candidate before you edit a model string
useCases.body: In OpenAI SDK code the model is a hardcoded string, and changing it is an act of faith. Replay last week's log first and read the verdict per step family, judged against outputs your users already accepted, before the string changes.

useCases.title: Cost per case from your logged usage
useCases.body: The report's cost per case sets what the winning candidate cost in replay against the recorded token usage of the same cases, priced at current list prices. If your wrapper also logs cost_usd and duration_ms, the adapter reads them, and rightmodeler drift uses them as cost and latency signals against the active replay corpus. Lines without them are still replayed.

limits: There is no export button for this format. The SDK does not write these logs by itself; your code does, by dumping each request and response as a line of JSON with a case_id attached. If yours does not yet, that wrapper comes first.
Every line needs case_id, a messages array, and a response object with a non-empty choices array. A line missing any of them is dropped with a recorded reason rather than guessed at.

Declared tools are not read from the request, and replay sends none, so cases from a call site that passes tools are left out of the replay sample. Replay sends recorded text conversations: a case whose input messages carry tool calls or content parts instead of a plain string is left out too, and the run says how many.

Evidence minimums are per evaluator kind: at least 10 assessed executions, at least two distinct step IDs, and at least five distinct trajectories. Below any of those the family abstains with a named reason instead of recommending.

Confirmation for coupled steps runs your pipeline in a container and needs a --modeb-config file naming the image and the step map. Without it the recommendation is reported as unconfirmed rather than quietly promoted.

It is not a runtime gateway. rightmodeler never sits between your SDK and OpenAI, and nothing changes in production until you merge the pull request. Confirmation runs your pipeline in a container that keeps the model key out but has ordinary network access, so point your app's tools at test fixtures, not production services.

faq.q: What does each line of the log need to contain?
faq.a: A case_id, a messages array, and a response object whose choices array is non-empty. model can sit on the line or on the response, usage on either, and timestamp orders the steps within a case. One JSON object per line, the request and its response together.

faq.q: I do not log my OpenAI calls today. What is the minimum?
faq.a: A thin wrapper around chat.completions.create that writes one JSON line per call: a case_id for the run, the request kwargs, and response.model_dump(). Most agent codebases already have a choke point every call passes through; that is the place.

Because the statistics cluster by trajectory. Cases from the same run are resampled together rather than counted as independent trials, so a ten-call agent run over five cases is not read as fifty. Without a case_id the adapter has nothing honest to cluster on, so it refuses the line.

faq.q: Does rightmodeler replace my observability setup?
faq.a: No. It runs offline, validating cheaper or newer candidates against the outputs you accepted and reporting the evidence for each call. If you later adopt LangSmith, Langfuse, or OTel GenAI, rightmodeler reads those traces too, same CLI, different adapter.

faq.q: My code hardcodes the OpenAI client. How can it confirm end to end?
faq.a: By running your pipeline in a container rather than patching your code. You name an image and a command in a --modeb-config file, your app is mounted read-only, and model calls leave through a metered proxy that swaps the model per step. Requests without a correlation header are refused rather than attributed by guesswork.

No, and that is the point. A family abstains when the evidence is thin or the excluded fraction runs over the ceiling, and nothing is proposed unless a candidate clears the quality floor on held-out cases. A tool that always finds a swap is not measuring anything.
